subject: paediatrics
title: Pediatric Nephritis and AKI: Complement, IgA, HUS, and Alport Syndrome

steps.tx: Selective activation of the alternative complement pathway produces distinctive serum complement profiles in pediatric glomerular diseases. Transient **hypocomplementaemia with low C3** is the hallmark of acute post-streptococcal glomerulonephritis, where C3 levels drop during acute presentation and normalize within six to eight weeks. Failure of C3 to normalize beyond eight weeks strongly indicates membranoproliferative glomerulonephritis (MPGN) or systemic lupus erythematosus.
steps.say: A low serum C3 level is characteristic of post-streptococcal glomerulonephritis, normalizing within eight weeks. Persistent low C3 beyond eight weeks indicates MPGN or lupus.

vis.alt: Microscopic histology of post-streptococcal glomerulonephritis showing diffuse proliferative glomerulonephritis with subepithelial humps.
vis.caption: Diffusely hypercellular glomerulus with subepithelial immune complex humps in post-streptococcal glomerulonephritis. [Credit: StewardMD]

steps.tx: Differential diagnosis of hypocomplementaemic versus normocomplementaemic glomerulonephritis narrows clinical suspect disorders effectively. While post-streptococcal nephritis, lupus nephritis, and membranoproliferative glomerulonephritis consume complement, conditions such as **normocomplementaemic pediatric glomerulonephritis** including IgA nephropathy, Henoch-Schonlein purpura nephritis, and anti-GBM disease demonstrate normal serum C3 and C4 concentrations throughout their active disease course.
steps.say: IgA nephropathy and Henoch-Schonlein purpura have normal C3 levels, whereas post-streptococcal nephritis and lupus cause low C3 levels.

steps.tx: Deposition of polymeric galactose-deficient IgA1 immune complexes within the glomerular mesangium defines the commonest primary glomerulonephritis worldwide. Characteristically presenting in school-aged boys, **pediatric IgA nephropathy** manifests with recurrent macroscopic synpharyngitic haematuria occurring concurrently or within twenty-four to forty-eight hours of an upper respiratory tract infection, accompanied by normal serum complement C3 levels.
steps.say: IgA nephropathy causes gross hematuria within forty-eight hours of an upper respiratory infection. Unlike PSGN, the latency is very short and complement levels are normal.

left.title: IgA Nephropathy (Berger Disease)
points: Normal serum complement C3 and C4

right.title: Post-Streptococcal GN (PSGN)
points: Subepithelial IgG and C3 humps on biopsy

steps.tx: Microangiopathic endothelial injury triggered by bacterial Shiga exotoxins precipitates a catastrophic triad of organ dysfunction. Following a prodrome of bloody enteritis caused by Escherichia coli O157:H7, **pediatric haemolytic uraemic syndrome** (HUS) manifests with microangiopathic haemolytic anaemia with helmet cells and schistocytes on blood smear, severe consumption thrombocytopenia, and oliguric acute kidney injury.
steps.say: Haemolytic uraemic syndrome follows bloody diarrhea from E. coli O157:H7. The triad comprises microangiopathic hemolytic anemia, thrombocytopenia, and acute kidney injury.

rows: RBC mechanical shearing in fibrin strands
Schistocytes on smear, high LDH, Coombs -
Transfuse packed RBCs if Hb <6-7 g/dL
Antibiotics provoke massive Shiga toxin release
Strictly supportive fluid and electrolyte therapy

steps.tx: Systemic leukocytoclastic small-vessel vasculitis mediated by IgA immune complexes affects skin, joints, bowel, and kidneys. Clinically presenting with dependent non-thrombocytopenic purpura, **Henoch-Schonlein purpura nephritis** develops in up to fifty percent of affected children, marked by microscopic haematuria and proteinuria identical to IgA nephropathy. The classic clinical tetrad includes palpable purpura, polyarthralgia, colicky abdominal pain with intussusception risk, and glomerulonephritis.
steps.say: Henoch-Schonlein purpura presents with palpable purpura, arthritis, colicky abdominal pain, and nephritis. Renal biopsy shows mesangial IgA deposition identical to Berger disease.

vis.alt: Clinical photograph of dependent palpable purpuric rash on lower limbs and buttocks in Henoch-Schonlein purpura.
vis.caption: Palpable non-thrombocytopenic purpura over lower extremities and buttocks in Henoch-Schonlein purpura. [Credit: StewardMD]

steps.tx: Genetic mutations encoding alpha chains of type IV basement membrane collagen produce progressive renal and sensory failure. Characteristically inherited as an X-linked dominant condition due to COL4A5 mutations, **pediatric Alport syndrome** presents with persistent microscopic haematuria in early childhood, progressive sensorineural hearing loss, anterior lenticonus, and renal failure in adolescent males. Electron microscopy shows basket-weave splitting of glomerular basement membranes.
steps.say: Alport syndrome is an X-linked collagen defect causing persistent microscopic hematuria, high-frequency deafness, and anterior lenticonus. Electron microscopy shows basement membrane splitting.

left.title: Alport Clinical Manifestations
points: Progressive proteinuria leading to ESRD in males

right.title: Genetic & Ultrastructural Pathology
points: COL4A5 gene mutation on X chromosome (85%)
Defective alpha-5 chain of type IV collagen
Basket-weave appearance of GBM on EM
ACE inhibitors slow progression of renal decline

steps.tx: Standardized international consensus criteria categorize acute renal deterioration based on creatinine elevations and urine output reductions. Diagnosis of **pediatric acute kidney injury** utilizes the KDIGO staging system, where Stage 1 represents a 1.5-fold serum creatinine increase, Stage 2 represents a twofold increase, and Stage 3 represents a threefold rise or serum creatinine exceeding four milligrams per decilitre, or initiation of renal replacement therapy.
steps.say: KDIGO stages acute kidney injury using serum creatinine elevations and urine output. Oliguria under 0.5 mL per kilogram per hour for six hours defines early injury.

rows: 1.5 to 1.9 times baseline or >=0.3 mg/dL rise
Adjust fluid intake; monitor electrolytes closely
<0.3 mL/kg/hr for >=24 hrs or anuria x 12 hrs

steps.tx: Distinguishing functional pre-renal hypoperfusion from intrinsic acute tubular necrosis guides aggressive fluid resuscitation versus strict fluid restriction. In **pediatric pre-renal versus intrinsic AKI**, pre-renal states exhibit intact tubular sodium reabsorption with fractional excretion of sodium (FeNa) below one percent, high urine osmolality exceeding five hundred milliosmoles, and prompt response to fluid boluses, whereas intrinsic tubular necrosis shows FeNa above two percent.
steps.say: Fractional excretion of sodium below one percent and high urine osmolality confirm prerenal azotemia. Intrinsic tubular necrosis causes fractional excretion over two percent.

left.title: Pre-Renal Azotemia Profile
points: Urine osmolality >500 mOsm/kg; responsive to fluids

right.title: Intrinsic Acute Tubular Necrosis
points: Muddy brown granular casts on urine microscopy
